newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt says Israel blocking peace efforts.
newsitem.headline: Egypt says Israel blocking peace efforts.

text.p: Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said in comments published on Thursday that his country's efforts at relaunching Israel-Palestinian peace talks were so far fruitless because of Israel's refusal to freeze settlements.

Moussa also told the government al-Ahram daily that the U.S. role in the Middle East peace process should be based on the principle of exchanging land for peace and on stopping Jewish settlements on occupied Arab land.
Egypt has recently taken on the mantle of main mediator in talks between Israel and the Palestinians.
President Hosni Mubarak's senior adviser Osama el-Baz has met separately with Palestinian and Israeli leaders several times in a bid to restart negotiations.

Baz also presided over a meeting between Israeli and Palestinian negotiators in Cairo earlier this month and held separate talks with the advisers this week, but both sides say there is still a big gap in their positions.
Asked about the results of Egypt's shuttle diplomacy, Moussa said:

"There are no results till now because of the Israeli position, particularly with regards to the question of settlements which are the main obstacle in the way of the peace process. The gap between the two sides is still large".

Substantive talks collapsed after Israel started building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March. The Palestinians want Israel to freeze settlement building before they return to the negotiating table but the Jewish state has so far refused.
Analysts say Egypt has stepped into the fray of Middle East diplomacy because the United States seems to have lost interest in the process.
Moussa said the United States was reassessing the Middle East peace process.

"We want an American position based on two things -- the principle of land for peace and stopping settlements. These two issues are the two most important foundations of the Middle East peace process," Moussa said.

"There is an absence of an American role right now. There are many reassessments in the current stage of the peace process, meaning reassessment of the peace process itself and the United States is immersed in reassessment," he added.

The Egyptian minister is currently on a European tour aimed at drumming up support for Egypt's initiative. He is due to accompany Mubarak in Paris on Thursday for a meeting with French President Jacques Chirac.
